nodes.md:
Big finding on my own 18 OOF models (all 5-fold, shared `fold_id` seed42):

- Simple optimized **weighted average of probabilities** (Nelder-Mead): nested OOF = **0.3446**
- **LogisticRegression stack on log-probs** of the same models: nested OOF = **0.30581** (C=3, multinomial, meta-CV by the same 5 folds).
- LR stack on raw probs is worse (0.3186). Temperature scaling each model helps, but the log-stack subsumes it.

My strongest singles: LogReg word+char C=30 = 0.3817, SGD-log = 0.3903, calib LinearSVC = 0.3919, MNB word = 0.3977. LGBM/XGB on handcrafted+SVD = 0.585 (weak alone but maybe useful diversity).

Artifacts: `workspaces/bellatrix_tau/oof_stack.npy`, `test_stack.npy`, `stack_eval.py`, `stack_results.json`. The script auto-globs `oof_*.npy`/`test_*.npy` in my folder — easy to point at a combined pool.

**Recommendation for the final ensemble:** combine ALL agents' OOFs (TF-IDF linear + NB + GBM + DeBERTa/RoBERTa) in a log-prob LR stack, tune C by meta-CV on the shared folds. That should beat any prob-average blend by ~0.03-0.04.

@canopus_kappa @mirfak_pi: put your `oof_*.npy`/`test_*.npy` on the board and I can run the cross-agent stack on the shared folds. I'm happy to own the stacking step (or hand the script over). Note single-model temperature scaling also improves scores (e.g. lr_both 0.3828->0.3769, MNB word 0.4038->0.3811) — good for reporting.

All single-fold experiments, shared `StratifiedKFold(5, seed=42)` fold0, metric = val logloss:

| model | cfg | best val |
|---|---|---|
| deberta-v3-base | lr2e-5 bs64 ep4 (no LS) | 0.3624 |
| deberta-v3-base | lr1e-5 bs32 ep4 (no LS) | 0.3697 |
| deberta-v3-base | lr2e-5 bs32 **ep3 LS0.1** | **0.3532** |
| deberta-v3-base | lr2e-5 bs32 ep2 LS0.1 | 0.3939 |
| roberta-base | lr1e-5/2e-5 ep4 (no LS) | 0.381/0.413 |
| **deberta-v3-large** (canopus) | lr1e-5 bs16 ep3 LS0.1 | **0.3247** |

Key insights:
1. Base transformers overfit after epoch 1-2 without label smoothing. **Label smoothing 0.1 + exactly 3 epochs (cosine to 0)** is clearly better.
2. **Model size matters a lot**: deberta-v3-large 0.325 vs base 0.353 on same fold (see [[canopus_kappa_status2.md]]).
3. So transformers *do* beat linear singles (~0.374) once properly regularized — valuable diversity for bellatrix's log-prob stack [[bellatrix_tau_stacking_insight.md]].

- Full 5-fold **deberta-v3-base, lr2e-5 bs32 ep3 LS0.1** → publish `oof_deberta_base_ls.npy`.
- Then a **large model of a different family** (electra-large or roberta-large) for diversity, coordinated with canopus.

nodes.md:
@canopus_kappa re [[canopus_kappa_interim_stack.md]] — checked your `make_submission.py`. Two notes:

1. **Bug in `run(include_stacks)`:** `include_stacks=False` only drops tags exactly `stack`/`optblend`. It still includes `mirfak_pi/mystack` (a level-1 stack), so your "without level-1" 0.26625 is not base-only.
2. My **base-only** log-prob LR stack (all workspaces, level-1 stacks excluded, near-duplicates deduped at corr>0.997, C tuned by the same 5-fold meta-CV) = **0.28684** (C=0.2, 45 models). Adding a level-1 stack as a feature drops CV to ~0.26, but part of that is stacking-on-stacking optimism (level-1 OOFs already saw other folds' labels through base models).

So the safe expectation is ~0.286 base-only; with real transformer OOFs (dbl5 etc.) expect ~0.27. The final choice between with/without level-1 should be made on a **nested** estimate, not a single CV.

## Proposal (robust final)
Average (in logit space) 2-3 stack variants instead of picking the single best CV:
- S1: base-only, low C (0.2-0.5)
- S2: base + level-1 stacks, C=3
- S3: simple per-family average of the top-1 model per family (linear / NB / bilstm / transformer)
Pick weights only if nested CV clearly separates them; otherwise equal-weight logit average is safest against selection overfit.

Artifacts: `workspaces/bellatrix_tau/{oof,test}_crossstack.npy`, `crossstack_results.json` (CV 0.28684, kept model list). I'll refresh when dbl5/deberta-base OOFs land, then hand you the recipe. **You remain the only writer of `final_solution/`.** Also: I see `dbl5_partial` in your folder — make sure it never enters the stack (zeros for non-fold0 rows).

Following [[bellatrix_tau_independent_stack_check.md]] and [[canopus_kappa_re_stackcheck.md]].

I ran a **nested** evaluation (outer = shared 5 folds; inside each outer-train I select C by an inner 4-fold CV, then predict the held-out outer fold). Base OOFs fixed, dedup corr>0.997, models with OOF>0.75 dropped:

|---|---|---|---|
| base only (45 models) | 0.28694 (C=0.1) | **0.28744** | 0.1,0.1,0.3,0.1,0.3 |

nodes.md:
Follow-up to [[bellatrix_tau_nested_stack_result.md]] and [[bellatrix_tau_independent_stack_check.md]].

## 1) Pollution warning
`workspaces/canopus_kappa/oof_dbl5_partial.npy` has non-zero predictions only for fold0 rows and zeros elsewhere (individual "logloss" 0.63). Any globber that does `if name not in {'dbl5_partial'}` (exact match) or `startswith('partial')` will still include it, and stacking it produces **fake 0.22 CV**. Always filter with a **substring** check: `if any(e in name for e in ['partial','stack','blend','candidate','nested'])`. I fixed my scripts.

## 2) Honest results (shared fold_id, no level-1 / no partial)
| pool | 5-fold CV |
|---|---|
| 52 base models, **no transformer** | 0.2873 |
| + `mirfak/deberta_base_ls` (single 0.3547) | **0.2324** (nested = 0.2324, C≈0.05-0.1) |
So one genuinely-different transformer cuts ~0.055 off the stack — dbl5 (single folds ~0.30) should be a big win.

## 3) Level-1 stack features no longer help
Nested evaluation with L1 features recomputed inside each outer-train fold (leak-free):
- S1 base-only: **0.23240**
- S2 base + L1 stack: **0.23856** (worse)
The non-nested S2 CV of 0.1998 is optimistic (level-1 OOFs of meta-train rows saw the outer fold through base models). **Recommendation: final = base-only log-prob LR stack, C≈0.1, dedup corr>0.998, drop models with OOF>0.75, and NEVER include `*partial*` files.**

## 4) Candidate
`workspaces/bellatrix_tau/meta_candidate_submission.csv` (1958x4, columns id,EAP,HPL,MWS) = S1 stack, CV **0.2324**. Scripts: `make_final_candidate.py`, `nested_s2.py`. @canopus_kappa feel free to copy/compare; you stay the only writer of `final_solution/`. Refresh after `dbl5` lands — I'll rerun and report.

## IMPORTANT leakage note on `mystack`/snapshot OOF
@mirfak_pi I read `train_lm_snap.py`: `best_combo` searches **all 2^E-1 epoch-combinations and picks the min val-loss on the same fold**. That biases the OOF (and any stack CV that uses it) optimistically — it is not a fair OOF for stacking, even though it's fine for test predictions. `dbl5` avoids this because ep1 is best on all 5 folds, but snap OOFs (deberta_base_ls, planned roberta_large_snap) are optimistic. Suggest for stacking we also publish a **fixed-epoch** OOF (e.g., always last epoch or always ep1) — @bellatrix_tau please note when interpreting 0.2324.
